gap_audit_against_r4_definition_of_done.conclusion: 2 of 9 items were genuinely missing (conflict-candidate detection; a named, jointly-evidence-producing reference corpus), 2 were partial (exact-duplicate policy; closure-test completeness), 5 were already done. This pass targets exactly the missing/partial items -- it does not re-litigate the 5 already-done items.

conflict_candidate_detection.what: SemanticObservation::subject_repr() (core/src/semantic/observation.rs) exposes each variant's typed payload via the same Debug-format component raw_observation_id() already used internally. runtime::normalize::detect_conflict_candidates groups typed_semantic_records by record_id (guaranteed same dimension, since SemanticRecordId embeds it) and flags any group whose members disagree on subject_repr() as a ConflictCandidate { record_id, dimension, raw_observation_ids } (core/src/schema/mod.rs), reported on NormalizationReport.conflict_candidates.
conflict_candidate_detection.deliberate_conservatism: Detection is full-payload-equality-based, not per-dimension-nuanced. This is intentionally OVER-inclusive (e.g. a future resolved-vs-unresolved difference on a non-identity field would also flag) rather than under-inclusive, because a false positive costs reconciliation one extra candidate to inspect while a false negative would silently hide a real disagreement -- the same asymmetry .atlas/contracts/NORMALIZATION.md's own epistemic-preservation rules apply elsewhere. A precise per-dimension conflict rule (distinguishing 'resolution progress' from 'genuine disagreement') is left as TARGET work, since zero real occurrence exists yet to design it against (see self_census_cross_check below) and guessing the boundary wrong risks a worse mistake than deferring it.
tests: runtime::normalize::tests::two_extractors_disagreeing_about_a_calls_resolved_targets_are_a_conflict_candidate (CallSiteIdentity.dispatch/callees, the exact 'extractor call-target sets' example NORMALIZATION.md's own Conflict handling section names)

exact_duplicate_accounting.what: normalize_typed_records now returns (Vec<SemanticObservation>, usize), the second element counting how many raw observations the existing raw_observation_id-exact dedup_by collapsed. Reported on NormalizationReport.exact_duplicates_merged.
exact_duplicate_accounting.closure_invariant_fix: NormalizationReport::typed_semantics_closed() previously asserted input_typed_closure.typed_observations_total == normalized_typed_closure.typed_observations_total -- an invariant that would have silently reported FALSE the first time real exact-duplicate collapse ever fired on a direct normalize() call bypassing build_census's own pre-dedup (build_census performs the identical collapse before typed_closure is even computed, which is why this gap was latent rather than already failing). Fixed to input == normalized + exact_duplicates_merged, matching .atlas/contracts/NORMALIZATION.md#closure-invariants verbatim ('input = normalized + explicitly represented exact-dedup equivalence').
exact_duplicate_accounting.still_bridge_not_target: This remains the narrowest safe case (byte-identical raw content, including evidence). NORMALIZATION.md's broader rule -- merging same-extractor observations that agree on identity+payload+status but differ in evidence, unioning the evidence -- is NOT implemented. Deliberately deferred: zero real trigger exists in any current Rust walker's output shape (each walker emits exactly one evidence ref per observation), and implementing a merge-with-union mechanism for an unexercised scenario would be speculative restructuring of a working, tested invariant for no evidenced benefit.

named_r4_reference_profile.what: R4_REFERENCE_PROFILE_CORPUS: one small, real, compiling-shaped Rust file combining already-proven-recognized constructs (a direct call, a branch, a let-binding def/use, a self.field read/write, a panic!, a shared &Widget borrow, .await, thread::spawn, and a commit() spelling) so it is evidence-producing -- not merely accounted -- for all 12 SemanticDimension variants simultaneously. Defined twice deliberately: once in adapter::semantic::rust::tests (proving the extractor boundary alone) and once in runtime::census::tests (proving the FULL canonical path: real extraction -> build_census -> normalize, using the real registered extractor via adapter::extractors_for_language, not a hand-built fixture).
named_r4_reference_profile.why_this_was_missing: .atlas/contracts/SEMANTIC-EXTRACTION.md#r4-definition-of-done's closing sentence requires naming 'the language/profile/reference corpus against which these gates were proven' for any project-wide R4-complete claim. Every existing corpus (CORPUS, CALL_CORPUS, CFG_CORPUS, DATA_FLOW_CORPUS, STATE_EFFECT_CORPUS, OWNERSHIP_CORPUS, CONCURRENCY_CORPUS, PERSISTENCE_CORPUS, ...) proves exactly one dimension or one wave in isolation; none was a single named artifact spanning all twelve together, so no R4-complete claim had one concrete corpus to point at.

bugs_found_this_pass.bug: NormalizationReport::typed_semantics_closed()'s equality check did not account for the exact-duplicate delta the contract's own closure-invariant formula requires -- latent (never triggered by any existing test or by build_census's own pipeline, which pre-dedups before typed_closure is computed) rather than actively wrong, but a real gap between the coded invariant and the contract text.
bugs_found_this_pass.fix: input_typed_closure.typed_observations_total == normalized_typed_closure.typed_observations_total + exact_duplicates_merged; proven by byte_identical_raw_observations_collapse_and_are_counted_as_exact_duplicates, which constructs a CensusReport directly (bypassing build_census) so the dedup genuinely fires inside normalize() itself, not before it.

closure_status.overall: R4.12 is MATERIALIZED, NOT FULLY CLOSED. 8 of 9 Definition-of-Done items are genuinely done; item 5 remains explicitly PARTIAL/BRIDGE, named rather than hidden, exactly like every other dimension-level 'closure remains open' status this roadmap already uses for R4.5-R4.11. overall_verdict: MATERIALIZED, NOT FULLY CLOSED. The two genuinely missing R4 Definition-of-Done mechanisms (conflict-candidate detection; a named, jointly-evidence-producing reference profile) are now real, tested at both unit and full-pipeline scope, and validated against this repository's own 25k-observation self-census with zero false positives. The one remaining partial item (the contract's full exact-duplicate equivalence-class rule) is named explicitly as BRIDGE/TARGET rather than silently left out or overclaimed as done. No new identity or epistemic model was introduced; ConflictCandidate and the exact_duplicates_merged count are purely additive reporting over the existing normalized-record architecture.

Per-dimension closure (R4.5-R4.11's individual 'closure remains open' statuses) is unaffected and unresolved by this pass -- R4.12 operates one level above those, on the PIPELINE's own guarantees, not on any single dimension's remaining Rust-construct coverage gaps.
